sections.body: This is a paper-trading research desk. Its 65 automated strategies and monitors cover US stocks, US exchange-traded funds and listed options (including index options), plus a set of paper-only crypto tests on coins such as Bitcoin, Cardano and Chainlink, all trading with pretend money on a paper account — no real money is at risk. The point is research: to test each strategy live, in real market hours, and record exactly what it does so the results can be studied honestly. This page is the public window into that desk. Everything shown here comes from the desk's own records, updated throughout the day.
sections.heading: What this desk is

sections.body: Here is one trade, end to end. A strategy's own rules spot a setup in the prices it watches — for example a stock breaking out of a tight range. The strategy states what it wants to do, but it cannot place an order itself: the request goes to the one Broker piece, the only part of the desk that talks to the paper account. The Broker sends the order, the broker fills it, and the fill — price, quantity and time — is written into the central record. This page is then built from that record together with the live paper account, so the account and position figures shown are the broker's own.
sections.heading: How a trade happens

sections.body:
Most prices come from Alpaca, the desk's broker. For fast-moving intraday data — especially anything that depends on trading volume — the desk uses Alpaca's full consolidated feed, which combines prices from all the major US exchanges.

Two kinds of prices do not come from Alpaca. The Tensor strategies — Tensor is the desk's name for its pattern-scoring engine, which grades stocks for swing setups — use hourly bars from Yahoo Finance, anchored to 9:30 a.m. New York time and locked to a single verified version of that feed. Every Tensor strategy reads from that same stream, and the system checks it has not changed before using it — so a Tensor result can always be traced back to the exact data that produced it. And the crypto tests price from the Kraken and Coinbase exchanges.

The VIX, the market's best-known fear gauge, also comes from Yahoo daily index data, because the broker does not carry that index. Each night, the desk also refreshes a research feed that mirrors the published work of ChartsLector, a chart researcher, and uses it as background context for the next day.
sections.heading: The data

sections.body:
The desk is built from seven core pieces. Each piece has one job:

- **Data** — Brings in prices through a small number of known sources — the broker for most prices, one locked Yahoo Finance feed for the Tensor strategies, and the Kraken and Coinbase exchanges for the crypto tests — so every strategy works from known numbers. If data is missing or stale, it is labelled as such rather than quietly used.
- **Strategies** — The 65 automated strategies and monitors. Each one checks its own rules against the prices and states what it wants to do — buy, sell, or wait. No strategy can place an order itself; every order goes through the Broker.
- **Broker** — The only part of the desk that talks to Alpaca. It sends orders, confirms fills, and handles the full life of an order from submission to completion.
- **Risk accounting** — Keeps the books on risk: how much each strategy holds, how much the desk holds in total, and how exposure is spread. The broker account holds the combined positions; this piece tracks which share belongs to which strategy.
- **Record** — One running record of every fill and every closed trade, written in order and never rewritten. The reviews on this page are read from it; the account and position figures are read live from the broker.
- **Scheduler** — The desk's clock. It wakes the right jobs at the right times — scans in market hours, reviews at night — so nothing depends on someone remembering to run it.
- **Terminal** — This page. It is a view over the record and the account, published fresh every 5 minutes during market hours, and it holds no numbers of its own.
sections.heading: The systems

sections.body:
Fifteen regular jobs keep the desk running around the clock:

- **Market scans** run repeatedly during market hours, giving each strategy its chance to act on fresh prices.
- **Exit sweeps** run every few minutes to check open positions against their sell rules, so exits are not left waiting for the next scan.
- **A premarket run** prepares the desk before the open each trading day.
- **This page refreshes every 5 minutes during market hours** with the latest account, positions, and activity.
- **A nightly reconciliation** compares the desk's own records against the broker's account, line by line.
- **A nightly review** writes up the day's closed trades — what worked, what did not, and why.
- **A nightly research refresh** updates the ChartsLector background feed.
- **A nightly market measurements run** recomputes the desk's market battery — breadth, the mood ring, risk appetite and theme rotation.
- **A gap-options check** refreshes the options data products the strategies read, on the scan cadence.
- **A nightly gap-products build** rebuilds the research data products (earnings, news, options and attention feeds) the strategies and setups read.
- **A heartbeat monitor** watches the desk itself: the desk regularly reports that it is alive, and a missed beat raises an alarm.
- **A nightly backup** saves a full copy of the desk.
- **Regular drills** — weekly practice runs that rehearse recovery, so restoring the desk is a tested routine rather than a hope.
- **A nightly archive** moves older sessions of the record into long-term storage and prunes them locally, so the live record stays lean.
- **Standing queries** run every 30 minutes. They check the stocks the desk follows against a fixed set of questions and note any name that newly matches.
sections.heading: The automations

sections.body: The desk is built so that its safeguards are structural, not a matter of remembering to be careful. It trades only on a paper account with pretend money. No strategy can place an order on its own: strategies can only state what they want to do, and every order reaches the broker through the one Broker piece described above — there is no second route in. And every action the desk takes is written, in order, to the one permanent record, which is only ever added to, never edited after the fact. That single, permanent record, together with the live broker account, is what this page is built from, and it is what makes the desk's results checkable.
sections.heading: Safety by design
